title: Law to let New Yorkers sue over unfair business practices
summary: This bill would let people and nonprofits sue businesses in court for unfair, deceptive, abusive or unlawful practices in trade or commerce, seeking damages of $2,500 per violation plus attorney's fees. It creates a private right of action not currently available under New York State law, with a requirement to notify the target in advance and a three-year time limit to sue. The law would not apply to the City, its agencies or employees, or small businesses with four or fewer employees and under $5 million in annual revenue.
